what: The tile layout this package publishes, held to bytes out of real cartridges rather than to a second reading of the same manual.
why: A decoder that misread the manual agrees with a record written from the same misreading, and agrees with itself over the whole input space. What separates a correct reading from a plausible one is data nobody here wrote: a picture read with the right layout has neighbours that match, and read with the wrong one it does not.
evidence: 11765 regions from 300 cartridges, chosen by where they sit rather than by what is in them, each read three ways. The published layout won 52.5% against a floor of 33.3%.
howToSettleIt: Settled for the tile layout at this depth. The other two depths, the palette and the map entry are still held to a second reading and to the whole input space rather than to cartridges.
